title: Video-LLaMA: An Instruction-tuned Audio-Visual Language Model for Video Understanding
grouping: Two side-by-side branches in dotted containers with bold serif titles in their top corners (Vision-Language Branch left, Audio-Language Branch right). Both start from one input box at the bottom that holds a row of video frame thumbnails above an audio waveform, and both end in a shared wide blue LLM box at the top. Text prompts and the generated answer sit in green dashed boxes around the LLM.
shapes_depth: Encoders are blue trapezoids; trainable blocks (Q-Formers, Linear) are orange rounded boxes, frozen ones blue rounded boxes. Per-frame features are drawn inside a rectangle as one rounded column per frame, each column a vertical stack of coloured squares (purple, green, yellow, red); audio features are tall blue bars. Above each column, a small grey box t_i and a circled plus show the per-position embedding added before the aggregator. Output tokens are a row of coloured squares in a rounded box. All text is serif (Times-like).
proposed_highlight: Trainable vs frozen is marked with icons in the box corners: a flame on the orange Q-Former and Linear boxes, a snowflake on the blue encoders and LLM; the two branches are given equal dotted containers.
lesson: Draw a video as a row of per-frame feature columns (stacked coloured squares, one column per frame), each tagged with a small timestep box t_i and a circled plus into the aggregator, so frame-wise position encoding is drawn instead of stated.
notes: Venue EMNLP from arXiv comment as reported by refs search; year = arXiv preprint year (2306.02858).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
